result:
Two branches share no common ancestor commit. Git refuses to merge them by default since 2.9, because it is usually a mistake.

Common causes:
- Local repo made with `git init` plus commits, remote made separately with its own README/license commit.
- Wrong remote URL, pointing at a different project.
- History rewritten or `.git` recreated on one side.
- Shallow clone (`--depth`) cut off the shared ancestor.

Check first:

```
git remote -v
git log --oneline --all --graph
```

Fix by case:

- **Histories really belong together** (e.g. fresh local repo plus remote with README): force the merge.
  ```
  git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories
  ```
  Resolve conflicts, commit. Same flag works on `git merge`.

- **Wrong remote**: fix URL, pull again.
  ```
  git remote set-url origin <correct-url>
  ```

- **Shallow clone**: fetch full history, retry merge.
  ```
  git fetch --unshallow
  ```

- **Local work not needed**: clone remote fresh, copy files in.

Replace `main` with your branch name.
